This is an amshu-vimarda (a collision of rays -- the discs themselves do not touch): center-to-center separation 0°38′08.22″, 0°38′03.77″ apart, disc-to-disc. aṅgārakaḥ at rēvatī-2 mīnaḥ (latitude 0°39′29.19″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude +1.10, elongation 3°57′45.84″ W). budhaḥ at rēvatī-2 mīnaḥ (latitude 1°17′37.42″ S, Rju (direct), magnitude -1.68, elongation 4°06′57.71″ W). Classical texts weigh both the northern position and the greater apparent brightness/nearness in deciding the victor (jayI) of a yuddha; here budhaḥ is towards the north (traditionally said to prevail), while by brightness/nearness (the larger apparent diameter) budhaḥ is taken as jayI over aṅgārakaḥ. A graha-yuddha (also called amshu-vimarda, "collision of rays") occurs when two of the five tArA grahas -- budha, śukra, aṅgāraka, br̥haspati, śanaiśchara -- come within 1 aMsha (60 kalA) of each other in longitude, close enough that they may be difficult to tell apart in the sky. It is called yuddha proper only when their discs actually touch/overlap; otherwise, amshu-vimarda.

The Surya Siddhanta itself cautions that this matter is described only to indicate the auspicious/inauspicious effects for people -- in reality the grahas remain far apart from one another and continue along their own paths. This is not to be received with fear, but as an advance, compassionate intimation from those who calculated these movements accurately, meant to help people take protective measures in time.

Classical texts (e.g. Brihat Samhita ch. 17) weigh both which graha is to the north and which is more prominent (nearer/brighter, of larger apparent diameter) in declaring a victor (jayī) of the yuddha; the defeated (jita) graha's significations are said to suffer for a particular section of society -- this is never a universal ill effect. The traditional response is to increase one's spiritual efforts: japa, homa, dAna and parAyaNa (especially of the Navagraha stotra), with higher AvRtti for the two grahas actually involved, particularly if the day also coincides with some other puNya kAla (e.g. a sAyana saGkramaNa).

Per the Narada Samhita (as cited in Muhurta Chintamani), the nakshatra in which a graha-yuddha occurs should be avoided for auspicious functions (vivAha, upanayana etc.) for six months following the event. If this cannot be avoided, perform parihAra for candra-bala.
3e49507c30.s:
bhāvābhāvāya lōkānāṁ kalpanēyaṁ pradarśitā।  
svamārgagāḥ prayāntyētē dūramanyōnyamāśritāḥ॥  
--sūryasiddhāntē

--muhūrtacintāmaṇau (nāradasaṁhitānusārēṇa)

3e89372262.b: Partial lunar eclipse (parimāṇa ≈3.8 of 12 aṅgulas), Moon at the Rahu node (puccha/descending).
3e89372262.d: The eclipse is already in progress at moonrise (grastodaya). Umbral magnitude: 0.32 (parimāṇa ≈3.8 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 09:38►19:53 (from 3 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra maghā/pūrvaphalgunī/uttaraphalgunī (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or pūrvāṣāḍhā (anujanma) or apabharaṇī (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: siṁhaḥ, kanyā, makaraḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ get more ashubha phala, dhanuḥ, kumbhaḥ, mēṣaḥ, karkaṭaḥ somewhat ashubha, tulā, vr̥śchikaḥ, mīnaḥ, mithunam shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.
3e89372262.r: - Food-restriction timing and graha-shanti nakshatra/rashi lists follow this pancAnga's "General notes for all grahanas" instructions.

saṅkrāntisnānākaraṇē pratyavāyamāha śātātapaḥ—  
sūryasaṅkramaṇē puṇyē na snāyādyadi mānavaḥ।  
saptajanmasu rōgī syād duḥkhabhāgī ca jāyatē॥

madhuśca mādhavaśca vāsantikāvr̥tū

nabhaśca nabhasyaśca vār‌ṣikāvr̥tū   
iṣaścōrjaśca śāradāvr̥tū   
sahaśca sahasyaśca haimantikāvr̥tū  
tapaśca tapasyaśca śaiśirāvr̥tū  
---taittirīya-saṁhitāyāṁ 4-4-11

3f1e40c294.d: The eclipse is already in progress at moonrise (grastodaya). Umbral magnitude: 0.42 (parimāṇa ≈5.0 of the traditional 12 aṅgulas). Avoid food: 09:24►19:53 (from 3 yaamas before the yaama of first contact, until the eclipse's end). Those with janma nakshatra maghā/pūrvaphalgunī/uttaraphalgunī (preceding/grahaNa/succeeding), or pūrvāṣāḍhā (anujanma) or apabharaṇī (trijanma) get ashubha phala and should consider graha-shanti next day. By rashi: siṁhaḥ, kanyā, makaraḥ, vr̥ṣabhaḥ get more ashubha phala, dhanuḥ, kumbhaḥ, mēṣaḥ, karkaṭaḥ somewhat ashubha, tulā, vr̥śchikaḥ, mīnaḥ, mithunam shubha phala. General notes: Avoid touching anything other than what's needed for the anushthana (especially bed/mat/cloth) until the mokSha snAna after the eclipse ends -- this is grahaNa Ashaucham. Do not sleep or attend to natural impulses during the eclipse. Mantra japa and dAna during the puNya kAla are of immense benefit. Do not view the eclipse with naked eyes. Pregnant women should avoid exposure to the sun/moon's light during the respective eclipse.

3fbaef4ed7.b: Event occured on 1704-01-06 (gregorian). Julian date was converted to Gregorian in this reckoning.
3fbaef4ed7.d:
Sikh Guru Govind Singh's  9 & 6 year old kids, Zorawar Singh and Fateh Singh, were killed by Mogols in Sirhind Fort. First they tried to bury them alive, then killed. They'd refusing to convert to Islam.

This verse is sung about them:

“Turk bhay mare naahin  
Hindu raha marhahi  
kaal sabhahun ko khai hai taantey ab tum vichaar karo chaar din Jeevan kay het hum dharma kyon gavaai hai.” 

> “We will not die just for the fear of Turks, we will remain Hindus till death, Time will kill all, why should we lose our Dharma for this life of four days.” 

- Panth Prakash, Giani Gian Singh.

**Timing**  
1705-01-07 gregorian = 1704-12-27 julian = pUrNimAnta pauSha 13 is mentioned. Their grandmother, Gurjar Kaur, also died on the same day or next, it seems.

A fair is held 11-13 Poh in commemoration. Indian government, under Narendra Modi, declared as vIra-bAla-divasa Dec 25 Gregorian in their memory - based on being bricked on Dec 25 Julian.

3fffe88dd7.d:
Between the 6th and 9th centuries, in South India, there existed 63 ardent devotees of Bhagavan Shiva, collectively known as the Nayanmars. These devout individuals, hailing from various walks of life including potters, fishermen, farmers, merchants, priests, hunters, and washermen, created devotional songs still sung by followers around the globe. Among these Nayanmars, Appar, Sambandar, and Sundarar, known for their Thevaram hymns, along with Manikkavasagar, are distinguished as the Samayacharyas or the ‘The Four’ (nālvar) revered teachers of the faith. They were instrumental in promoting the Shaiva Siddhanta philosophy and culture, effectively challenging the spread of Jainism and Buddhism. Their teachings centered around the concept that Shiva embodies love, and that embracing love for all beings and existence is essential in connecting with Shiva, the Supreme Being.

The 43rd Nayanmar was a Vaishya, and resided in Pennagadam, a part of the Chola kingdom. He was known for his devout service in the local temple and held a deep reverence for Shiva Bhaktas, seeing the divine presence of Bhagavan Shiva in them. His wife also actively supported him in these spiritual endeavours.

On one occasion, though, a man who had previously been a servant of the Nayanmar visited his house, disguised as a Shiva Bhakta. True to his devotional nature, the Nayanmar warmly welcomed the visitor, offering the traditional respect of washing his feet and venerating him. However, his wife, recognizing the man as their former servant, did not participate in the worship with the same enthusiasm.

Perceiving his wife's reluctance as a lack of devotion, the Nayanmar, in a drastic and shocking act, severed her hand. He then proceeded to continue his worship of the disguised Bhakta with undeterred focus. Through this extreme form of spiritual practice and dedication, he ultimately achieved union with the divine.
3fffe88dd7.r: - 63 Nayanmar Saints by Swami Sivananda, published by The Divine Life Society
